exposure: Time periods: pre-COVID (January 2018-January 2020), elective postponement (February-May 2020), recovery (June-November 2020), and postrecovery (December 2020-December 2021)
Three emergency procedures: Caesarean section (CS), emergency laparotomy (EL), and open fracture (OF) fixation
cohort: Patients who underwent emergency Caesarean section, emergency laparotomy, or open fracture fixation between January 1, 2018 and December 31, 2021
finding: Elective surgery postponement in the early COVID-19 pandemic did not affect volumes of emergency Caesarean sections and open fracture fixations but led to an increase in volume for emergency laparotomy after the postponement without any worsening of outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no change in weekly volumes of Caesarean sections across the four time periods.
